issues.description: Dataclass field uses forward-string type without resolvable import context
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service is typed as a string forward reference "FrameProcessor", but FrameProcessor may not be importable in frames.py (likely creates a circular import). Even if dataclass doesn't evaluate it at runtime, get_type_hints() and tools like pydantic/serializers will fail. Prefer importing under TYPE_CHECKING or using Any.

issues.description: service field has no default, breaking any existing call sites that constructed the frame with no args
issues.detail: The prior RequestMetadataFrame() was constructible with no arguments. Anything outside this PR that instantiates it (user pipelines, plugins, tests) will now raise TypeError. A field default of None plus a None-check in push_frame would preserve backward compatibility for the rename.

issues.description: Equality check on FrameProcessor instance may misbehave for dataclass __eq__/__hash__
issues.detail: ControlFrame is a dataclass; adding a FrameProcessor field means dataclass-generated __eq__ will compare processors structurally, and __hash__ becomes None unless eq=False is set. This can break sets/dicts holding these frames and cause surprising equality. Mark the field with field(compare=False) or set eq=False on the dataclass.

issues.description: Suppression logic leaks frames targeted at inactive services downstream
issues.detail: push_frame only consumes the frame when frame.service == active_service. If a frame targets an inactive service (e.g., misrouted, stale, or from a future caller), it now escapes downstream where nothing handles it. Safer to always consume ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame in the switcher regardless of target.

issues.description: Breaking rename has no deprecation alias for downstream users
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame was a public symbol in pipecat.frames.frames. Removing it outright will break third-party code at import time with no migration window. Consider keeping `RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` with a DeprecationWarning for one release.

issues.description: Comment is stale after behavior change in STTService
issues.detail: The old comment said "Don't push the RequestMetadataFrame, just push the metadata" — the new behavior does push it. The replacement has no comment explaining the ordering invariant (metadata first, then the request frame). Add a brief note so future readers know the order is intentional and contract-bound.

review.summary: The rename plus targeting field is a reasonable refactor, but the new `service: \"FrameProcessor\"` field introduces several risks: missing default breaks any existing zero-arg constructors, dataclass-generated __eq__/__hash__ semantics change in a way that affects set/dict use, and the forward-string type may fail under get_type_hints or trigger circular imports. The switcher's new conditional suppression can also leak frames targeting non-active services downstream. Consider an aliased deprecation for the old symbol and a stale-comment cleanup in STTService.
